articles.title: 'She's back': Fans dance, sing and cry after Céline Dion's comeback concert in Paris
articles.summary: Thousands turned out to witness Céline Dion perform in Paris on Saturday, her first show after a six year illness-induced hiatus.
articles.body:
Céline Dion's first concert in years delighted fans, with the Canadian singer crying as she made an emotional comeback to the stage.

It was Dion's first full concert in six years after she was diagnosed with a rare neurological disorder called stiff person syndrome, which forced her to cancel tours.

Joyful fans spilled out of the Paris La Défense Arena on Saturday night singing and dancing to her classic hits, while some were still wiping away tears.

Paris correspondent Hugh Schofield went along and reflects on getting swept up in the Dion dalliance that French fans are calling "the biggest comeback since Charles de Gaulle".

articles.title: Vento derruba placa sobre motociclista em Quixeramobim; vídeo | G1
articles.standfirst: A vítima, Francisco José Rufino, contou ao g1 que não sofreu fraturas graves, mas teve escoriações nas costas, nas mãos e nos pés. O caso ocorreu neste sábado (12) em Quixeramobim.
articles.summary: A vítima, Francisco José Rufino, contou ao g1 que não sofreu fraturas graves, mas teve escoriações nas costas, nas mãos e nos pés.
articles.body:
Uma forte rajada de vento derrubou a placa de um comércio e o letreiro caiu sobre um motociclista que passava pela Rua Castelo Branco, em Quixeramobim , no interior do Ceará, por volta do meio-dia deste sábado (12). A cidade fica a cerca de 200 quilômetros de Fortaleza.

A vítima, o agricultor Francisco José Rufino, de 54 anos, contou ao g1 que não sofreu fraturas graves, mas teve escoriações nas costas, nas mãos e nos pés . O capacete que ele usava partiu ao meio com o impacto.

Francisco disse que tinha ido a uma farmácia comprar um medicamento quando foi surpreendido pelo vento forte.

“Foi uma coisa que nem sei como aconteceu tão rápido desse jeito. Eu estava em um supermercado e um senhor pediu para eu comprar um remédio para ele na farmácia. Fui na minha moto. Cheguei, comprei e vinha saindo. Foi tão ligeiro. De repente formou aquele redemoinho na pista. Parei a moto no acostamento, porque vinha um carro na minha frente. Quando me dei conta, veio só aquela pancada em cima de mim. Caí com moto e tudo”, relatou.

Funcionários da loja ajudaram a vítima. — Foto: Reprodução

Após o acidente, testemunhas levaram o motociclista a uma Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA), onde ele passou por exames, incluindo raio-X. Em seguida, foi liberado após receber atendimento médico.

“A minha salvação foi o capacete, porque, se não fosse o capacete, eu não estava contando o que eu estou contando”, afirmou Francisco.

Um vídeo de câmera de segurança registrou o momento em que a placa despenca. As imagens também mostram o vento forte assustando outras pessoas na rua.

Placa de loja cai sobre motociclista. — Foto: Reprodução

Uma delas foi Osvaldo Almeida, dono da loja de peças de moto responsável pela placa. Segundo ele, a queda aconteceu em poucos segundos.

“A placa caiu, eu nem percebi. Os meus funcionários é que correram para socorrer o rapaz”, disse. Francisco é cliente antigo da loja. Osvaldo afirmou que prestou apoio à vítima após o acidente.

“O que for preciso eu resolvo. A placa é minha, só que eu não tive culpa. Mas ele é um cliente meu há muito tempo”, declarou.

Segundo o empresário, ele pagou um capacete novo, a reposição das peças danificadas da moto e os medicamentos necessários para a recuperação do cliente. “Ficou de boa, graças a Deus, tudo resolvido”, concluiu.

articles.title: Cadeirante de 7 anos chega ao topo de serra com a família; vídeo | G1
articles.standfirst: Laura Leite, que usa cadeira de rodas desde os 3 anos, realizou o sonho de alcançar o tradicional Cruzeiro de Santo Antônio, símbolo religioso e cultural em Campo Maior.
articles.summary: Laura Leite, que usa cadeira de rodas desde os 3 anos, realizou o sonho de alcançar o tradicional Cruzeiro de Santo Antônio, símbolo religioso, após subida com 1.840 degraus.
articles.body:
Até onde vai o amor? A resposta para familiares e amigos da pequena Laura Leite, de 7 anos, pode parecer simples: ao topo . Cadeirante, a menina chegou ao topo da Serra de Santo Antônio, em Campo Maior , no Piauí, a 402 metros de altitude, após percorrer 1.840 degraus.

Ainda antes do nascimento, Laura foi diagnosticada com mielomeningocele , quando a coluna vertebral não se desenvolve completamente. Ela passou por uma cirurgia intrauterina para corrigir a condição, mas ficou com sequelas e, aos 3 anos, passou a usar cadeira de rodas .

Laura mora em Timon (MA), mas viaja com frequência para Campo Maior, onde parte da família vive. Desde a construção das escadarias da Serra de Santo Antônio, os passeios ao ponto turístico passaram a fazer parte dessas viagens.

"A gente subia a serra praticamente todos os anos e sempre sonhava em levar a Laura até o topo. Quando conseguimos, foi uma alegria muito grande para toda a família", disse a mãe, Marina.

O sonho virou realidade no dia 6 de setembro. Para isso, familiares e amigos se mobilizaram.

Cadeirante de 7 anos supera 1.840 degraus e chega ao topo de serra com ajuda da família no PI — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Um dos principais apoiadores foi Gustavo, amigo da família, que aceitou participar da subida. Durante o percurso, ele, Marina, o pai da menina, Guilherme, e a madrinha, Tathyane, se revezaram para conduzi-la na subida.

Em imagens compartilhadas nas redes sociais, Laura aparece sorrindo durante o percurso e celebrando ao chegar ao alto da serra.

A conquista teve um significado ainda maior

Na 22ª semana da gestação, os pais descobriram que Laura tinha mielomeningocele, quando a coluna vertebral não se desenvolve completamente. Na 26ª semana, Marina passou por uma cirurgia intrauterina para corrigir a condição.

Apesar do procedimento, a menina ficou com algumas sequelas, como bexiga neurogênica hiperativa e falta de força nas pernas, e passou a utilizar cadeira de rodas aos 3 anos.

"Desde muito nova, incentivamos ela a ser independente. Sempre buscamos dar autonomia para que ela pudesse fazer as coisas do dia a dia da maneira dela", contou Marina.

Hoje, aos 7 anos, Laura está no 2º ano do ensino fundamental, faz terapias em Teresina e, segundo a família, é uma criança esforçada e dedicada aos estudos.

Além da conquista na Serra de Santo Antônio, Laura e a família mantêm outro objetivo.

Há cerca de dois anos, parentes e amigos promovem campanhas para arrecadar recursos para um tratamento com células-tronco no Paraguai. Segundo a família, o procedimento pode contribuir para melhorar a qualidade de vida da menina.

O tratamento custa cerca de 25 mil dólares e é dividido em três aplicações. Até a última atualização da reportagem, o valor necessário para iniciar o procedimento ainda não havia sido arrecadado.

Parque Estadual da Serra de Santo Antônio

O Parque Estadual da Serra de Santo Antônio, situado no município de Campo Maior, no norte do Piauí, abriga trilhas ecológicas, cachoeiras e áreas de floresta preservadas, sendo propício para caminhada, ciclismo e até rapel

O grande desafio para quem visita o local é encarar a escadaria com 1.840 degraus, a maior do Nordeste e uma das maiores do país, que conduz ao tradicional Cruzeiro de Santo Antônio, símbolo religioso e cultural da cidade.

A subida, que pode durar cerca de três horas e meia, exige preparo físico, mas recompensa o visitante com uma vista panorâmica marcada por paredões de arenito e pela riqueza natural da região.

articles.title: Motoristas têm prejuízos após veículos caírem em buracos na RJ-114, em | G1
articles.standfirst: Pelo menos sete veículos ficaram parados às margens da rodovia na noite desta sexta-feira (11), na altura de Ubatiba; trecho recebeu reparo emergencial com asfalto frio.
articles.summary: Pelo menos sete veículos ficaram parados às margens da rodovia na noite desta sexta-feira (11), na altura de Ubatiba; trecho recebeu reparo emergencial com asfalto frio.
articles.body:
Motoristas tiveram prejuízos depois que vários veículos caíram em buracos na RJ-114, rodovia que liga Maricá a Itaboraí, na Região Metropolitana do Rio. Os problemas foram registrados na noite desta sexta-feira (11), na altura de Ubatiba, em Maricá.

Um vídeo feito no local mostra pelo menos sete carros parados às margens da rodovia, todos com o pisca-alerta ligado. Na manhã deste sábado (12), a equipe do g1 esteve no trecho e encontrou alguns dos buracos tapados.

O serviço foi feito de forma emergencial pela Autarquia de Serviços de Obras de Maricá (SOMAR). As Equipes utilizaram asfalto frio ainda na noite de sexta-feira para reduzir o risco de novos acidentes.

Apesar da atuação emergencial do município, a RJ-114 é uma rodovia estadual, e a responsabilidade pela conservação é do Departamento de Estradas de Rodagem do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (DER-RJ).

Procurado pela equipe do g1, o DER-RJ informou que retomou os serviços de conservação nas rodovias estaduais e que a RJ-114 está incluída na programação. O Órgão informou ainda que equipes técnicas v percorrer a estrada para atualizar o levantamento das condições do pavimento após as chuvas recentes e identificar os pontos mais críticos, que serão priorizados nas intervenções.

articles.title: Idoso morre após ser atropelado por moto em Santarém; condutor fugiu sem prestar socorro | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima de 64 anos atravessava a rua para comprar pão quando foi atingida, segundo a família. Homem fazia tratamento de hemodiálise e sofreu quatro paradas cardíacas após o acidente.
articles.summary: Vítima de 64 anos atravessava a rua para comprar pão quando foi atingida, segundo a família. Homem fazia tratamento de hemodiálise e sofreu quatro paradas cardíacas após o acidente.
articles.body:
Hospital Municipal de Santarém — Foto: Kamila Andrade/g1

Um idoso identificado como Raimundo Lopes, de 64 anos, anos morreu após ser atropelado por uma motocicleta em Santarém , no oeste do Pará. Segundo a família, ele atravessava a rua para comprar pão, pouco antes das 7h, quando foi atingido pelo veículo. O motociclista fugiu sem prestar socorro e, de acordo com os familiares, deixou o local levado por outra pessoa.

A vítima foi socorrida pelo Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) e encaminhada ao pronto-socorro municipal. Um vizinho que atua como bombeiro foi quem avisou a família sobre o atropelamento.

Segundo a esposa, o idoso fazia tratamento de hemodiálise e havia saído de casa mais cedo que o habitual naquele dia. Ao encontrá-lo no hospital, ela percebeu que ele sentia fortes dores.

"Ele dizia muito que estava doendo na omoplata. Eu apertei e chegou a chiar, como se tivesse bem quebrado. Eu ficava dando massagem nele com a mão no peito e no braço para acalmar", relatou.

Exames realizados no hospital apontaram quatro fraturas na região da bacia. Por causa da condição renal, segundo a família, a administração de medicamentos para controlar a dor chegou rapidamente ao limite permitido.

Durante a manhã, o estado de saúde do idoso se agravou. Ele apresentou febre, sofreu convulsões e precisou ser levado para a sala de reanimação.

A vítima teve quatro paradas cardíacas consecutivas. A equipe médica conseguiu reanimá-la após a primeira parada, mas o idoso não resistiu às demais e morreu no início da tarde.

A família cobra responsabilização pelo atropelamento e pela fuga do motociclista sem prestar socorro.

articles.title: Criança e adolescentes ficam feridos em incêndio após carro pegar fogo | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítimas foram socorridas pelos responsáveis e levadas a hospital, de acordo com os bombeiros.
articles.summary: Caso aconteceu neste sábado (12), em Jaboatão dos Guararapes, no Grande Recife. Vítimas foram socorridas pelos responsáveis e levadas a hospital, de acordo com os bombeiros.
articles.body:
Três pessoas ficaram feridas após um carro pegar fogo e causar um incêndio numa casa em Jaboatão dos Guararapes, no Grande Recife . Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, as vítimas são uma criança e dois adolescentes. Os nomes e as idades dos jovens não foram divulgados.

O caso aconteceu na tarde deste sábado (12), na Rua Marrocos, localizada no Loteamento Grande Recife, no bairro de Sucupira. Imagens que circulam nas redes sociais mostram as chamas se espalhando no imóvel (veja vídeo acima) .

De acordo com os bombeiros, o fogo começou no veículo, que estava na garagem da residência, e se propagou dentro do imóvel, atingindo uma parte do terraço.

A corporação informou que, após ser acionada, enviou ao local três viaturas e controlou o incêndio, isolando a área e fazendo o rescaldo em seguida.

Ainda segundo os bombeiros, as vítimas foram socorridas pelos responsáveis e levadas a uma unidade de saúde antes da chegada das equipes de resgate. A corporação disse também que, diante dos danos causados no imóvel, interditou preventivamente a casa e acionou a Defesa Civil.

Como os nomes das vítimas e a unidade hospitalar não foram confirmados, não foi possível confirmar o estado de saúde delas.

articles.body: A snake-eating king cobra had just taken its unusual meal to another level. In a garden in Karnataka, a nearly 12-foot-long king cobra was found in the process of swallowing a python, leaving the family who spotted it with a scene that looked almost unreal.The incident took place on Friday evening, September 11, in Kading, Tenkakarandur village in Belthangady taluk. According to reports by Mangalore Today, the family spotted the giant cobra in their garden and alerted local snake rescuer Ashok.But the most startling part came during the rescue.As the rescuer carefully worked to move the snake to safety, the king cobra regurgitated the python it had swallowed. The cobra was then safely captured and released in a forested area, according to the reports.A king cobra eating a python is not as strange as it soundsThe image may be shocking, but the meal itself fits the king cobra's biology remarkably well.Unlike most snakes, king cobras are specialists in hunting other snakes. Their scientific genus name, Ophiophagus, essentially means “snake-eater”. Their diet can include both venomous and non-venomous snakes, and documented prey includes cobras, kraits, rat snakes and pythons.That makes the python less of an accidental meal and more of the kind of prey a king cobra is evolutionarily equipped to pursue.The king cobra is also the world's longest venomous snake, with individuals capable of growing beyond five metres. Its size gives it an advantage when confronting other snakes, while its venom helps subdue prey before it is swallowed whole.Why can a snake swallow another snake whole?The answer lies partly in the extraordinary flexibility of a snake's skull.Snakes do not have jaws that are fused together like ours. Their highly flexible jaw structure allows them to stretch around prey that appears impossibly large compared with their heads. Once the prey is subdued, the snake gradually works it into its mouth and down its throat.For a king cobra, this adaptation is particularly useful because its prey is often another long, flexible snake.And there is another surprising detail: king cobras can consume a very large meal and then go for extended periods without eating again. Their relatively slow metabolism means a successful hunt can provide a substantial energy reserve.The python was not necessarily an easy opponentA python is not helpless prey. Large pythons are among the few snakes capable of challenging a king cobra, and encounters between the two can be dangerous for both animals. The king cobra's advantage comes from being a specialised snake predator, but size and physical strength still matter.That is one reason the Karnataka rescue is more than a bizarre wildlife sighting. It captures a rarely witnessed part of the food chain: one of India's most formidable predators taking on another large snake in a battle for survival.The incident also shows why rescuers caution people against approaching such scenes themselves. A king cobra may normally avoid humans, but a snake that has been disturbed while feeding or being handled can become highly defensive.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: Brics hammers out joint declaration after India bridges Iran-UAE chasm
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: In a dramatic repeat of the 2023 G20 Declaration under India’s presidency, Brics member-states reached a consensus for a joint declaration .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In a dramatic repeat of the 2023 G20 Declaration under India’s presidency, Brics member-states reached a consensus for a joint declaration following intensive, late-night negotiations that lasted till 4 am on Saturday. The talks had been strained by sharp differences between the UAE and Iran over the West Asia conflict and an earlier meeting of the Brics foreign ministers under India’s presidency had ended without a consensual statement.Also Read | Iconic moments, landmark talks & a breakthrough pact: Key points from Brics SummitThe 140-paragraph New Delhi Declaration announced by PM Narendra Modi was solidified by a rare leader-level Iran-UAE meeting - between Iran President Masour Pezeshkian and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan – in the middle of the war that started on February 28.In a delicately worded compromise, the declaration addressed the interests of both sides by expressing serious concerns over deliberate attacks on civilian infrastructure and also peaceful nuclear facilities under full safeguards of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), in violation of international law and relevant resolutions of the IAEA. This implicit criticism of US-Israeli action against Iran was crucial in getting Iran to sign off on the declaration.“We in Brics must fight against the normalization of attacks on civilian, vital infrastructure. The same applies to peaceful nuclear infrastructure," said Pezeshkian at the summit​​​.Nuclear safeguards, safety, and security must always be upheld, including in armed conflicts, to protect people and the environment from harm, said the declaration.Significantly, the joint statement did not name any country or explicitly condemn attacks, prioritising instead dialogue and diplomacy, UN Charter, civilian lives and infrastructure and respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States, while also expressing deep concern over continued escalations and calling for maximum restraint.Also Read | 'India can be bridge-builder': UN hails Iran-UAE meeting on sidelines of BricsIn the declaration, the leaders recalled their respective national positions on West Asia and stressed the need to work together to maintain smooth flow of global trade, supply chains and energy, in accordance with applicable international law.Official sources said India led prolonged negotiations at multiple levels to reconcile sharp differences between the 2 sides and forge consensus with support from other member-states who were keen that the summit didn’t end without a joint statement.The Brics consensus is reminiscent of the last-minute G20 2023 Delhi declaration that was achieved in the middle of the escalating Russia-Ukraine war with a carefully nuanced formulation that called upon all States to refrain from use of force for territorial acquisition but without naming Russia.The Brics declaration also came days before Iran’s meeting with GCC countries on the Strait of Hormuz situation. In Pezeshkian’s meeting with the crown prince, the leaders underscored the importance of supporting efforts to ease tensions, promote de-escalation and strengthen regional stability.Indian officials had on Friday expressed confidence about a constructive outcome from the negotiations, following Modi’s meeting with Pezeshkian in which he expressed solidarity with Tehran, seeking a long-term and win-win partnership with Iran.On other issues, like in Rio last year, China and Russia, as permanent members of the UN Security Council, reiterated their support to the aspirations of Brazil and India to play a greater role in the UN, including the Security Council.Importantly for India, the declaration expressed strong condemnation of any acts of terrorism as “criminal and unjustifiable, regardless of their motivation, whenever, wherever and by whomsoever committed” and strongly reiterated condemnation of the Pahalgam terrorist attack.“We reaffirm our commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including the cross-border movement of terrorists, terrorism financing and safe havens,” said the declaration.On the Palestine issue, Brics countries, including India, expressed deep concern on the continued violence in Gaza despite the ceasefire agreement of October 2025. “We call for halting any policies aimed at forced displacement of Palestinians from Gaza Strip and express concern regarding arrangements that may prejudice the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people and legitimize or prolong occupation,” said the declaration.There was no mention of the Ukraine war in the declaration this year. The declaration backed comprehensive reform of the UN, including the Security Council, with a view to making it more “democratic, representative, effective and efficient” and to increase the representation of developing countries in the Council's memberships.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Tens of thousands march across Germany to protest far-right party AfD
articles.summary: Protesters in about 20 cities, including Berlin, Hamburg and Munich, demand the banning of the Alternative for Germany.
articles.body:
Tens of thousands of people took to the streets across Germany to protest against the Alternative for Germany (AfD) after the far-right party won a state election by a landslide.

About 150,000 demonstrators turned out in roughly 20 cities on Saturday, including Berlin, Hamburg and Munich, in rallies organised by Pruef, a campaign group pushing for a ban on the AfD.

Protesters carried signs reading “Ban the AfD now” and “Democracy needs no alternatives.”

“A broad cross-section of civil society is taking to the streets to prevent the enemies of the constitution … from gaining government power,” said Christoph Bautz, head of Campact, another campaign group involved in the protests, which put turnouts at about 25,000 in Hamburg and 12,000 in Munich.

According to police, several thousand more joined separate demonstrations in Berlin.

The AfD held its own counter-rally in the German capital, attended by Kristin Brinker, the party’s lead candidate for Berlin’s upcoming regional election.

The protests follow a stunning result for the AfD in Saxony-Anhalt, a state in eastern Germany, where the party took nearly 44 percent of the vote on September 6 — far ahead of the roughly 17 percent won by Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s Christian Democratic Union (CDU), which has long dominated German politics.

The AfD, known for its anti-immigration stance and friendly posture towards Russia , fell just short of an outright majority and is now in talks with other parties to try to form a government, which would make it the first far-right party to lead a German state since the Nazi era ended in 1945.

AfD state leader Ulrich Siegmund called the result historic, telling supporters: “The people have made it absolutely clear that they finally want political change and, above all, they have shown that they want it with us.” He has since signalled openness to working with other parties, after previously saying he wanted to govern alone.

The AfD’s growing strength has deeply unsettled many Germans, given the country’s history and its commitment to never repeating it.

The party is projected to win 39 of 83 seats in the state parliament, three short of a majority. It now needs a coalition partner, though all mainstream parties have so far refused to govern with the AfD under a longstanding policy known as the “firewall.” The far-right party has never joined a governing coalition anywhere in Germany, at either state or national level.

The unease has fuelled growing calls to ban the AfD altogether, though that would be legally difficult in Germany, and Chancellor Merz has been reluctant to pursue it.

articles.title: Diljit Dosanjh: Punjabi singer makes history under the famous Wembley arch
articles.summary: Wembley Stadium billed Diljit Dosanjh as the first Punjabi singer to headline the iconic music venue.
articles.body:
On Saturday night, under the world-famous Wembley arch, five words rang out: "Punjabi Aa Gaye Wembley Oye!"

Indian megastar Diljit Dosanjh famously starts all his concerts by announcing that "the Punjabis have arrived".

But this time, it was a play on the usual catchphrase.

Dosanjh is the first ever Punjabi singer to headline Wembley Stadium, the music venue has said.

Addressing his fans, he reflected on the significance of the occasion. "This moment will go down in the history books," he said.

And as Bhangra beats blared out, fans erupted with cheers while Dosanjh launched into his biggest hits, from G.O.A.T. to Lover.

Over two decades, Dosanjh has built a huge global fanbase, topping charts and singing with the likes of Ed Sheeran.

He has even busted Bhangra moves with Jimmy Fallon , with the US talk show host labelling him "the biggest Punjabi artist on the planet".

His landmark concert at Wembley further cements his status as a global star.

Ahead of the show, the singer spoke exclusively to the BBC backstage, describing the moment as "a dream" for him.

In London, Dosanjh's crowd was largely - but not entirely - South Asian.

The hype for his appearance was building all afternoon, with fans arriving early to get in place.

"MJ [Michael Jackson] and Madonna, he's that level for us," said one fan. "He's so good looking, and so down to earth," said another.

When he came on the stage shortly after 8pm, dressed in traditional attire, the stadium erupted and the screams barely stopped for the next two-and-a-bit hours.

Known for his high-energy performances, he wowed fans with his dance routines to songs including Hass Hass and Born to Shine.

His soulful voice echoed around the stadium, demonstrating his range, as he blended homegrown Punjabi music with rap and hip-hop.

Throughout the show, the audience waved lights, sang along and - of course - danced. At times, the standing area closest to the stage resembled an Indian wedding, with fans copying Dosanjh's impressive moves.

But despite performing in such a vast venue, Dosanjh proved again his ability to connect on a personal level with fans.

He brought a range of fans on stage, from young children to an elderly woman, taking selfies and giving them gifts.

He also acknowledged those in the back rows of the 90,000-seater stadium, saying those at the back were "full of heart", and encouraged applause for them.

There was also exciting news for fans in India, as he announced he would be performing in November at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad.

The concert was capped off with the emotion of the night - his track Main Hoon Punjabi, which means "I am Punjab" - set to a spectacular firework display.

"What an incredible show, the energy and vibe was unparalleled!" concert goers Amit and Rani told the BBC.

"We love Diljit and have been to all his shows in the UK. This was something else, a moment in time we won't forget being a part of."

They added that it was not only a privilege "but a moment to celebrate for Punjabi culture".

From Coachella to Fallon: Decoding Diljit Dosanjh's stardom

From humble beginnings as a small village boy from Punjab, he made history in 2023 by becoming the first Punjabi-language singer to perform at the US music festival Coachella.

He also famously made his Met Gala debut decked in majestic Punjabi attire.

His meteoric rise has seen him perform across America and Europe, and collaborate with pop stars from Sia to Sheeran.

His authenticity is a big part of his appeal. He remains true to his Punjabi roots, wears his turban as a sign of pride, and sings in his mother tongue.

Away from music, Dosanjh is also a popular Bollywood actor - and a social media sensation. Even those who haven't heard his music have probably viewed his funny Instagram videos - such as him arguing with an Amazon Alexa device that couldn't understand his accent.

Now, he's performed on a stage that's previously been home to titans of music from Taylor Swift to Coldplay.

For Dosanjh and his millions of global fans, it means Punjabi music, Punjabi culture and Punjabi vibrancy has reached an historic moment.

Speaking to the BBC before his gig, he said he felt "thankful" to be here.

"When we were going to book this venue, everyone said, 'Think again before you book, it's a big stadium'," he said.

"I said: 'We'll see whatever comes. I want that our people are happy and can say yes, we can do this too!'"

He reflected on the many artists who had performed there before him, adding that to follow their footsteps "means a lot, a lot".

"It may not mean as much for someone like Harry Styles, as much as it means for us. He has performed on such stages, but for us, it's very special. Coming from a village to here - it's very special."

"I feel good. I feel happy. And I feel good for my people. I feel good for the next generation," he said.

And of course, there was only one way he could end.

articles.title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England
articles.summary: Changes will spell out that governments can change rules and that career choices affect repayments.
articles.body:
University applicants in England will be given clearer information about student loans before they take them out, the government has said.

Ministers said they would spell out that governments can change repayment rules and that different career choices can affect how much borrowers repay.

They agreed to some but not all of the recommendations made by MPs after an inquiry into student loans, and did not say whether they would reverse a freeze to the repayment threshold for some graduates.

The inquiry found the way loans had been presented to teenagers amounted to mis-selling , after the BBC revealed the Department for Education (DfE) had compared repayments to £30-a-month phone contracts.

The recent debate has centred around Plan 2 loans, which were issued in England between September 2012 and July 2023, and are still issued in Wales.

The interest rate on those loans is the Retail Prices Index (RPI) measure of inflation plus up to 3% depending on earnings, and borrowers repay at a rate of 9% of everything they earn over a repayment threshold, which is meant to rise with inflation every year. The loans are written off after 30 years.

Campaigners want a lower interest rate, a lower repayment rate and for the government to reverse a decision last year to freeze the threshold at £29,385 for three years in England.

Freezing that threshold means graduates start repaying their loans sooner and, once they do, they pay more than they would have done if it had risen with inflation.

MPs on the Treasury Committee called for a U-turn on that decision as part of a series of recommendations after an inquiry this summer.

The Treasury and the DfE did not say whether ministers would unfreeze the threshold in their response, but said: "We keep all aspects of the student finance system under review."

The government rejected recommendations to:

Split the cost of university evenly between the student and the government

Stop using RPI to calculate interest rates

Ensure promotional materials comply with Financial Conduct Authority's Consumer Duty, saying student loans were "very different to commercial loans"

However, it agreed to "making it more prominent that... regulations may be amended by government and Parliament".

It also said "more can be done to help student loan borrowers understand how their loan balance may change over the long term".

The government also said giving students long-term predictions of how much they might ultimately repay risked being "misleading" because of "limited" accuracy.

It proposed instead to "demonstrate how different life and career choices may affect repayment trajectories", including salary progression, retraining, part-time work, and career breaks.

How student loans work for tuition fees and living costs

'Deeply misleading' school talks compared student loans to £30 phone contracts

Phone contract comparisons 'amounted to mis-selling' student loans, MPs say

Students starting university in England now have Plan 5 loans, which have a lower interest rate but also a lower threshold and longer repayment term.

Nick Hillman, director of the Higher Education Policy Institute, who helped design the Plan 2 system, said the government had "absolutely rejected" most of what the Treasury Committee had recommended and its response would not meet the concerns of Plan 2 graduates.

Oliver Gardner, founder of the Rethink Repayment campaign, said the government's response "does not go far enough" and he wanted to see "concrete action" in the autumn Budget.

While Dame Meg Hillier, chair of the Treasury Committee, said making information clearer was "an important step" but "doesn't help graduates who are angry that they didn't receive the same service and are now facing punitive repayment terms on a loan which keeps growing".

She urged the chancellor to reverse the threshold freeze in this autumn's Budget.

In March, a BBC investigation found that as well as comparing monthly student loan repayments to phone contracts, the government told presenters to "avoid words [or] phrases like debt" during presentations in schools across England a decade ago.

More than 120 MPs and peers recently signed a letter coordinated by the campaign group Rethink Repayment calling for an "urgent review" of the system.

One of the signatories, Liberal Democrat MP Tom Gordon, who is a Plan 2 borrower, is set to introduce a bill calling for a review in Parliament next week.

Education Secretary Lucy Powell has previously said the interest rate on Plan 2 loans was "egregious" and the issue was at the top of her in-tray.

The Student Loans Company said it was working with the government to "provide clear, relatable and trusted guidance".

articles.title: Dad dies after horrifying cruise ship accident while celebrating his son’s wedding
articles.summary: Pastor Steve Junker of Minnesota suffered a spinal cord injury and nearly drowned in a pool aboard the Sun Princess cruise ship while celebrating his son's wedding in Italy.
articles.body: A pastor from Elbow Lake, Minnesota, has died after suffering a severe spinal cord injury during a cruise in Italy while celebrating his son's wedding. Steve Junker was aboard the Sun Princess on Aug. 16 when he fell and was later found face down and unresponsive in a pool, according to a GoFundMe page organized by his family. Princess Cruises said ship personnel were alerted on Aug. 16 that a passenger needed medical assistance. "The guest was attended to by the ship's medical team and subsequently transferred ashore for further care," the cruise line said. Junker's family said he suffered a spinal cord injury and nearly drowned during the accident. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER He was transported by an Italian Coast Guard boat to a hospital in Naples, where he was admitted to the intensive care unit, according to the fundraiser. Junker underwent emergency spinal surgery the following day. His family said the procedure was successful, though his spinal cord injury remained severe. As Junker remained hospitalized, his family said they faced challenges navigating his medical care overseas and worked to arrange transportation to a hospital in the United States. "We are working through the medical, logistical and financial challenges of arranging appropriate medical transport and getting him to a hospital in the United States," the family wrote before his death. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES He was ultimately taken to Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota, on Aug. 23 for additional medical treatment, according to reports. The family asked friends and loved ones to keep Junker in their thoughts and prayers. "Thank you from the bottom of our hearts for every prayer, message, phone call, kind thought, and offer of support," the family wrote. He ultimately passed away on Sept. 4 surrounded by loved ones, according to family postings on Facebook. "Pastor Steve was a wonderful person, loved by many, and had a great impact on many people through his faith," Chippewa Lutheran Church wrote in a Facebook post. Junker's church remembered him for his faith. The church also shared a tribute from Nathaniel Junker, Steve Junker's son, who sang worship songs inspired by his father. "He closed his eyes to this life and opened his eyes to Jesus," the church's post read. Fox News Digital reached out to Junker's family for comment. An obituary for the pastor noted that he worked as a pharmacist before answering the call to ministry. He left behind a wife, five children and their spouses, a grandchild and many other family members.

articles.title: Tom Felton: I'm so excited to see Rupert Grint play Ron Weasley again
articles.summary: Tom Felton talks about taking on Broadway, Rupert Grint following his footsteps and a new Harry Potter generation.
articles.body:
Every night on Broadway, Tom Felton walks on stage and is met with a roar from the audience. He had expected the reaction to die down after the first week, but it never did.

Almost 15 years after his final appearance as Draco Malfoy on screen, Felton has spent the past 10 months playing the character again in the Broadway production of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child.

I meet the actor in a dressing room at NBC Studios, just off Times Square in New York. He's just finished a live television appearance and in a few hours will be back on stage for his next performance.

He greets me with a hug and says he is excited to speak to BBC News because his mum and 100-year-old grandfather will see it. His family are some of his biggest supporters - his mum has seen the show five times already, while his dad is due to visit next month.

That support mirrors the enthusiasm Felton has encountered from Harry Potter fans, which he says still surprises him more than two decades after he first played Draco.

"I thought the applause would stop in the first week and it has not.

"It's very humbling and lovely to know how much the characters still mean to people now and if it brings them to the theatre, that's the best."

He is also struck by how many of the fans now approaching him were not alive when the first Harry Potter film was released.

"There are fans that approach me shouting 'Draco' who weren't even born when I was in the first film," he says.

Felton was the first of the original Harry Potter cast to reprise his role in the theatre show, but he will not be the only one for much longer, as Rupert Grint is set to reprise his role as Ron Weasley on Broadway in February.

The 38-year-old actor says he called his former co-star as soon as he heard the news.

"We are typically - and he will agree with me - pretty bad at our phone game, but when I heard the news I called him immediately and I'm so excited for him" Felton says. "Who doesn't want to see Rupert Grint play Ron Weasley again? Come on!"

I ask whether Felton offered any advice to his co-star but he laughs and says absolutely not, pointing out that Grint has already appeared on Broadway.

"I don't think he needs any advice from me. If anything, I would be taking it from him."

He adds that Grint has a "Ron Weasley laissez-faire approach to these things".

More than two decades after they first met on the Harry Potter set, Felton says the friendships between the young cast have endured.

He describes Grint, Daniel Radcliffe and Emma Watson as "best mates" and "family", even if getting them all in the same place is now difficult.

"We are usually in four different corners of the earth, so it's hard to get together," he says, adding that their support since his return to Draco has been "fantastic".

As Felton and Grint return to familiar roles on stage, a new generation is preparing to take over the characters in HBO's television adaptation of the books set to air later this year.

Felton recently met his successor, Lox Pratt, and "saw a lot of myself in him".

Felton says he was struck by Pratt's confidence and describes him as a "charming young man and fabulous actor".

"My mum is in contact with his mum and I'm encouraging him to be as cheeky as possible - but professional first."

Felton says he is not worried about the level of scrutiny Pratt and the other young actors may face as they take on some of the best-known characters in popular culture.

"I'm not worried about that at all for him. He's got a very good head on his shoulders and what you don't know doesn't hurt you. I'm sure he's not one to scroll through negative comments."

Nor does Felton appear concerned that Harry Potter is being adapted again relatively soon after the films.

Instead, he says the longer television format offers the chance to explore parts of the books that the films did not have time for.

"We had two hours to fit in a lot of content and the wizarding world is vast, so it's exciting to know they can dive in deeper."

"I hope the fans of the books and films explore more about Draco," he says.

While some actors might want to distance themselves from the role that made them famous, Felton has embraced his connection to Harry Potter.

He says the franchise has given him "a life I could never have imagined" and that, even today, it is "bringing people together from every corner of the earth".

Asked whether this really is the last time he will play Draco, Felton is reluctant to rule anything out.

"I suppose I said 15 years ago that was the end of Draco and I was leaving him forever, but here I am.

"It's hard to say with any certainty what's to come."

articles.title: Death toll from Philippine ferry fire rises to 76
articles.summary: The Philippine Coast Guard says 41 more bodies have been recovered from the M/V June Aster, with 13 people still missing
articles.body:
The death toll from a Philippine ferry fire has risen to 76, with 13 people still missing, after search teams recovered additional remains from the passenger vessel off Palawan province.

The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) said in a statement on Saturday that 41 more charred bodies were retrieved from the ferry.

The MV June Aster was sailing from Manila, carrying 132 passengers and crew, when a blaze engulfed its lower decks on Wednesday evening, just 2.2 kilometres (1.3 miles) off its destination of Coron, in northern Palawan.

Rescuers pulled 43 survivors from the water that night.

Investigators, citing survivor accounts, reported hearing successive explosions before flames swept rapidly through the passenger areas.

“The wind may have contributed to the rapid spread of the flames, based on the survivors’ accounts,” said Commodore Noemi Cayabyab, spokesperson for the PCG, according to local media outlet the Inquirer.

“Some passengers reportedly jumped into the water after seeing the fire and may not have had time to retrieve their life jackets.”

According to authorities, forensic teams and local police are working to identify victims using personal belongings and DNA matching.

“The PCG, [the Philippine National Police’s Scene of the Crime Operatives] and other concerned agencies are currently undertaking the proper recovery and identification of the remains in accordance with established procedures,” Cayabyab said.

Safety procedures and the ship captain’s actions during the early minutes of the disaster are under formal review, maritime officials said.

“With the number of missing and the number of capacity, definitely there is liability here,” Cayabyab added regarding the vessel’s command.

The ferry’s operator, Atienza Interisland Ferries, issued a statement committing to “full transparency” and assisting affected families with lodging, transportation and medical care as investigations continue.

articles.title: Russians seek answers over hundreds missing after Ukraine's 2024 incursion
articles.summary: Officials say more than 300 Russians remain missing after the 2024 Kursk offensive, but no-one really knows the true figure.
articles.body:
"I used to have complete faith in our country," says Lyubov. The last time she spoke to her mother was a day after Ukrainian forces broke into Russia's Kursk region more than two years ago.

Now she feels "resentful towards the [Russian] state", in a country where most people avoid criticising the full-scale invasion unleashed on Ukraine in February 2022.

The local governor says more than 300 Russians are still missing in Kursk region, but no-one really knows the true figure.

Lyubov says she tried to persuade her mother to leave her village in the Sudzha area, but blames Russian state TV "propaganda" for her refusal to listen. Some 2,000 people remained in the settlements captured by Ukraine's military, Russian authorities estimate.

"The state channels were convincing viewers that 'everything is under control: two or three days, and it'll be just as it was before'," she recalls.

She still fails to understand why Russian authorities could not stop Ukrainian soldiers storming two border checkpoints in August 2024, taking around 40 prisoners and bombing a convoy carrying Russian soldiers.

Within six days they had overrun more than 777 sq km (300 sq miles) of Russian territory, as Ukraine's military sought to divert Russian forces away from their front-line offensive.

For most of the next eight months, mobile and internet links were down.

Russia's foreign ministry repeatedly accused Ukraine of war crimes against civilians: allegations rejected in Kyiv as completely unfounded .

Nearly 200 Russians sent a letter to Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky, Russia's President Vladimir Putin and the United Nations, asking them to organise a humanitarian corridor to evacuate civilians.

It never happened and, by late autumn, battles raged as Russian forces sought to retake the territory.

Lyubov and others who had lost contact with their loved ones began to form groups.

One resident, whose family friends had also stayed behind, began compiling a list of people she saw on videos published by the Ukrainian military and journalists. Then she began detailing those believed to have died and where they were buried.

"At first, in a panic, you try to do something – anything – to find some sort of information," she said. "Taking action brings a certain sense of relief, and that's how you can cope with the stress."

Soon about 1,000 names were on the list.

Lyubov wrote to the Red Cross and Kursk interior ministry appealing for help, but had no response.

Early in 2025, Russia's human rights commissioner published a list of 517 Kursk residents reported missing. The list mixed up names of the missing with those who were searching for them, and the families said it was like a "slap in the face".

"Publishing something like this is the height of incompetence and a lack of basic respect for people," said one young woman whose parents had gone missing, in a video shared online.

Heavy fighting had been reported in late 2024 in the village of Darino, where Lyubov and mother were from, and authorities said that 90% of it had been destroyed.

The Russian military regained control of the village and then began evacuating those who had survived, and the bodies of those who had not.

One of the evacuees got in touch with Lyubov, telling her she had lived with her mother for the past few weeks. Her mum had passed away, she explained, following a head injury in circumstances that remain unclear.

A few other elderly people had also died, she said, unable to cope with wartime conditions.

Lyubov waited in vain for her mother's body to be brought out, while other families had no idea if their relatives were alive or dead.

People complained no-one was searching for their loved ones and that there was no single list of those missing.

Lyubov heard that the bodies of neighbours who died alongside her mother had been taken away from Darino in April, but her mother's body was still missing.

She tried and failed to get an answer from the authorities: "They wouldn't listen, and everyone just kept saying that it was dangerous there, and no-one was going to deal with it right now."

The head of one local village council, Yuri Tkachev, was among volunteers who went to retrieve the bodies of civilians, from the streets or from nearby fields.

"It's hard for people to know – or rather not to know – what has happened to their loved ones, whether they're being held captive or have died, and where they died," he said.

Body bags and fuel for vans taking part in the evacuations were paid for either by the volunteers themselves or with donations, but not by authorities.

Although regional officials met the group searching for the missing several times in the second half of 2025, relatives complained it made little difference.

Lyubov was still searching for her mother's body, until she visited the mortuary last October during a trip to the regional capital Kursk.

"I just asked: 'A woman born in 1949 from the village of Darino – are there any unidentified bodies?'"

The official turned his laptop screen towards her and immediately she recognised her deceased mother in a photograph from April 2025.

She was lying on her side in the street, her knees bent. Lyubov tried not to look too closely. She recognised her mum's face and an old jumper, which she wore while she worked.

She had provided a DNA sample in January but was told it had been lost, so her mother's body had been in the mortuary unidentified for several months.

She had wanted to bury her mother in their home village, but for now that is impossible, so she has been cremated and her ashes sit in Lyubov's apartment in Belgorod, about 100 miles away.

She is bitter that the government failed to stop the incursion, that it did not evacuate residents when it could, and that it persuaded them the situation was not serious.

Asked by the BBC to comment on this story, there was no response from the Kursk governor, Russia's human rights commissioner or the Russian Red Cross.

The command of Ukraine's Territorial Defence Forces and Ukraine's human rights commissioner of Ukraine said all the civilians they had evacuated from Kursk region had been handed over to Russia.

Lyubov thinks back to when she used to ride her bike across the border into Ukraine to shop for sausages, yarn and ice cream.

"We went to see them, and they came to see us. And now not one of these villages exists any more."

articles.title: Especialista explica como limpar mofo e alerta para risco de misturas | G1
articles.standfirst: Profissional com mais de 10 anos de experiência recomenda evitar pano seco e misturas caseiras. Ventilação adequada é essencial para resolver o problema.
articles.summary: Profissional com mais de 10 anos de experiência recomenda evitar pano seco e misturas caseiras. Ventilação adequada é essencial para resolver o problema
articles.body:
A combinação de períodos frios e chuvosos, comuns nesta época do ano no Rio Grande do Sul, aumenta a umidade nas residências, o que favorece a proliferação de mofo em banheiros e atrás de móveis . Para combater o problema, o recomendado é o uso de produtos puros e evitar misturas caseiras .

O especialista em higienização doméstica Cássio Siqueira Nunes, que atua na área em Santa Maria há mais de uma década, explica que há um método simples para remover os fungos.

"O que é correto para a limpeza de mofos? Principalmente usar um detergente neutro e usar também um pano úmido. Justamente para não proliferar o mofo e limpar ele bem na sua essência", afirma.

Nunes destaca que o pano nunca deve estar seco na hora da faxina , pois isso faz com que o mofo se espalhe pelo ambiente. A orientação é aplicar o detergente neutro ou a água sanitária sempre com o tecido umedecido.

Uma prática comum na internet, mas desaconselhada pelo profissional, é a criação de misturas caseiras, como unir água sanitária com vinagre, álcool ou desinfetantes .

"Nós não aconselhamos fazer nenhum tipo de mistura, justamente porque os produtos são industrializados e o pessoal confunde muito e coloca água sanitária com vinagre, água sanitária com álcool. Não se mistura. Usa sempre o produto puro", alerta.

Após a remoção da sujeira, é fundamental secar a superfície afetada.

"Não adianta apenas limpar. Depois de limpar, tirar o mofo, é secar o local. O mofo vem decorrente da umidade, então quanto menos úmido e mais seco o local, melhor", orienta o especialista.

A prevenção também envolve mudanças na organização da casa, já que o mofo se desenvolve em locais com umidade e pouca ventilação. A recomendação é afastar os móveis das paredes , especialmente as que fazem divisa com a área externa. Nos banheiros, a orientação é manter as janelas abertas após o banho para garantir a circulação do ar.

Para espaços menores e fechados, Siqueira sugere o uso de produtos específicos. Em guarda-roupas e closets, os potes antimofo vendidos em mercados e farmácias são essenciais. Já para as gavetas, a dica é utilizar pacotes de sílica-gel. "Numa gaveta, num lugar de pequena circulação, ajuda um monte", conclui.

A professora Camila Baldasso, do curso de Engenharia Química da Universidade de Caxias do Sul (UCS), explica que o fungo está sempre presente no ar, mas precisa de condições específicas para crescer. "A gente tem o combo: calor, poeira, fungo, que é o mofo, e umidade que vem desse processo."

Para controlar a propagação do mofo, ela sugere estratégias práticas para a limpeza , como uso de vinagre, água sanitária e cloreto de cálcio.

Detergente: passar um detergente neutro e usar um pano úmido para retirar as manchas. É preciso usar luvas.

Vinagre de álcool: a recomendação é borrifar o produto puro sobre a região com mofo, deixar agir por cerca de uma hora e limpar com um pano úmido. O uso de luvas e máscara é obrigatório.

Água sanitária: indicada para azulejos e vidros, devendo ser evitada em superfícies porosas. O produto precisa ser diluído em água na proporção de um para um. Exige uso de luvas e máscara devido à toxicidade, especialmente em ambientes fechados como banheiros.

Cloreto de cálcio: esferas químicas que sugam a umidade podem ser colocadas em pequenos potes dentro de guarda-roupas.

Desumidificadores: aparelhos eletrônicos que retiram a umidade do ar também são opções, embora exijam maior investimento financeiro.

articles.title: São Paulo terá domingo chuvoso e frio após temporal causar alagamentos e deixar desaparecidos | G1
articles.standfirst: Capital registrou 75,4 mm de chuva em 24 horas, maior volume do país no período; Jardim Pantanal, na Zona Leste, voltou a ficar debaixo d’água e cidades da Grande SP tiveram deslizamentos e alagamentos.
articles.summary: Capital registrou 75,4 mm de chuva em 24 horas, maior volume do país no período; Jardim Pantanal, na Zona Leste, voltou a ficar debaixo d’água e cidades da Grande SP tiveram deslizamentos e alagamentos.
articles.body:
São Paulo terá um domingo (13) chuvoso e frio após um sábado marcado por alagamentos, transtornos no trânsito e ocorrências graves na capital e na Grande São Paulo . Em Jandira, dois homens estão desaparecidos depois de serem arrastados pela correnteza de um rio durante a madrugada.

Segundo a previsão do Climatempo, deve chover durante todo o domingo, durante o dia e também à noite. A temperatura deve ficar entre 14ºC e 16ºC.

A chuva deste sábado (12) provocou alagamentos em diferentes pontos da capital e da Grande São Paulo. No Mirante de Santana, na Zona Norte, o Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) registrou 75,4 milímetros em 24 horas, o maior volume de chuva do país no período, segundo a Defesa Civil.

Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, um deles estava em uma área alagada quando foi arrastado pela correnteza. O outro homem e a irmã, de 32 anos, tentaram ajudá-lo, mas também foram levados pela água. A mulher conseguiu se agarrar a árvores às margens do rio e foi socorrida.

Ela contou que a correnteza ficou forte de forma repentina.

“Foi, foi minutos. Foi muito rápido. Entendeu? Na hora que eu fui levada, parece que a onda veio do nada e me levou, sabe? Porque não tava tão forte assim.”

Até a última atualização, os dois homens ainda não haviam sido encontrados.

No sábado, a Defesa Civil Municipal recebeu 34 chamados, entre 6h e 18h. Foram 14 ocorrências de quedas de árvores, 12 para desabamentos e oito para deslizamentos.

3 de fevereiro - Moradores do Jardim Pantanal, na Zona Leste de São Paulo, enfrentam terceiro dia seguido de inundações no bairro, que sofre há décadas com os problemas das enchentes. A região com cerca de nove bairros fica numa área de várzea do rio Tietê — Foto: Fábio Vieira/FotoRua via Estadão Conteúdo

Na região do Jardim Pantanal, na Zona Leste de São Paulo, ruas e casas voltaram a ficar alagadas neste sábado.

Quartos, cozinhas e salas foram tomados pela água. Moradores levantaram móveis para tentar salvar os pertences.

Durante a enchente, bombeiros resgataram um homem acamado e o levaram para um local mais seguro.

O distrito tem 45 mil moradores, fica dentro do Jardim Helena e é uma área de várzea que se estende por nove bairros ao longo da Zona Leste, divisa com Guarulhos. Localizada na beira do Rio Tietê, a área é onde justamente o rio corre devagar e faz curvas.

A região deveria ser uma Área de Proteção Ambiental (APA), em que são proibidas construções de casas e ruas. Contudo, a ocupação irregular e desordenada da cidade transformou a região em um bairro de muitas famílias e comunidades.

Moradores também reclamaram de uma obra na Rua Macapera e disseram que a situação teria piorado depois da intervenção.

“Colocaram uns tubo aí, mas ao invés da situação melhorar, piorou, jovem, piorou. Quando chove, a água entra na casa, não tem como sair”, disse o aposentado Antonio de Oliveira.

A Prefeitura de São Paulo afirmou que as obras na Rua Macapera não têm relação com os alagamentos na região do Jardim Pantanal. Segundo a administração municipal, galerias de microdrenagem foram implantadas para ajudar no escoamento das águas.

A Prefeitura também informou que a Guarda Civil Metropolitana Ambiental estava no local com viaturas e botes para auxiliar os moradores.

O temporal também provocou problemas no trânsito da capital.

Na Marginal Tietê, um alagamento bloqueou as pistas sob as pontes das Bandeiras, Casa Verde e Freguesia do Ó, no sentido da Rodovia Castello Branco.

Segundo a Companhia de Engenharia de Tráfego (CET), o congestionamento chegou a 564 quilômetros às 13h30, o segundo pior índice da semana, atrás apenas de quinta-feira.

Durante a tarde, parte das pistas foi liberada, mas a pista central continuava interditada e a pista expressa, próxima ao Rio Tietê, seguia com tráfego lento.

Na Rodovia Régis Bittencourt, na altura de Itapecerica da Serra, houve alagamentos no sentido da capital. Motoristas chegaram a entrar na contramão para conseguir passar.

Outras cidades da região metropolitana também registraram ocorrências.

Em Cotia, o centro de treinamento das categorias de base do São Paulo Futebol Clube ficou alagado. Uma partida do Sub-15 foi suspensa no intervalo, enquanto os jogos do Sub-17 e do Sub-20 foram adiados.

Em Juquitiba, alagamentos e deslizamentos atingiram diversos bairros. Segundo a prefeitura, 60 casas foram interditadas e 50 pessoas ficaram desalojadas. Um abrigo provisório foi montado para receber os moradores.

Em Santo André, houve quedas de árvores e desabamentos, sem registro de vítimas graves.

O governo do estado anunciou ajuda aos municípios atingidos pelas chuvas.

Segundo a Defesa Civil do Estado, São Paulo vive um dos setembros mais chuvosos desde 1943.

Na capital, o acumulado do mês já está entre os maiores da série histórica, embora setembro ainda esteja na primeira metade.

A sequência de chuva também mantém as temperaturas baixas na cidade.

A explicação apresentada para o período chuvoso é a atuação de frentes frias mais frequentes sobre o estado, em um cenário associado ao El Niño.

Nos anos de 1983 e 1993, também houve episódios de El Niño forte e setembros muito chuvosos em São Paulo.

A orientação é que moradores acompanhem os alertas da Defesa Civil e evitem áreas sujeitas a alagamentos durante os períodos de chuva.

articles.summary: Quinze pessoas foram resgatadas com vida; governo investiga possível sobrecarga da embarcação e falha no cumprimento de alertas marítimos.
articles.body:
Pelo menos uma pessoa morreu e mais de 30 estavam desaparecidas neste domingo após uma balsa afundar na costa de Vanuatu, informou em nota o gabinete do primeiro-ministro Jotham Napat.

As operações de busca e resgate continuavam na nação insular do Pacífico, localizada a cerca de 1.750 quilômetros a leste da Austrália, após o naufrágio do MV Matui com dezenas de tripulantes e passageiros a bordo, segundo o comunicado publicado no Facebook.

Quinze pessoas foram localizadas com vida, acrescentou a nota.

As buscas estavam em andamento desde que a embarcação que fazia transporte entre ilhas afundou durante uma tempestade na sexta-feira entre as ilhas de Ambae e Santo, de acordo com a emissora pública neozelandesa RNZ.

O gabinete de Napat informou que a busca em mar aberto está sendo reduzida, enquanto os esforços se concentram na costa sudeste, para onde as correntes marítimas podem ter levado sobreviventes.

"Esta tragédia parece ser resultado de ventos fortes e do descumprimento de alertas marítimos, além de possível negligência, incluindo a sobrecarga da embarcação", diz a nota.

"Aos sobreviventes, desejamos força e recuperação. Às famílias dos desaparecidos e das vítimas, saibam que a nação está ao lado de vocês neste momento de luto", acrescenta o comunicado, informando que uma investigação será conduzida.

Matai Seremaiah, representante da região de Luganville no Parlamento de Vanuatu, afirmou que os trabalhos de resgate começaram após um tripulante do MV Matui chegar à costa nadando e alertar as autoridades.

"Ele nos avisou que a embarcação havia virado. Então iniciamos as buscas", disse Seremaiah em declaração transmitida pela RNZ.

A polícia de Vanuatu, a Autoridade de Segurança Marítima de Vanuatu e a operadora da embarcação, Tui Shipping Agency, não responderam imediatamente aos pedidos de comentário.

articles.title: Mega-Sena pode pagar R$ 85 milhões neste domingo; g1 transmite ao vivo | G1
articles.standfirst: Apostas simples podem ser efetuadas até as 22h de sábado. Já os Bolões CAIXA nos canais eletrônicos ocorrem até as 10h45.
articles.summary: Apostas simples podem ser efetuadas até as 22h de sábado. Já os Bolões CAIXA nos canais eletrônicos ocorrem até as 10h45.
articles.body:
O concurso 3.057 da Mega-Sena pode pagar um prêmio de R$ 65 milhões para os apostadores que acertarem as seis dezenas. O sorteio ocorre às 11h deste domingo (6), em São Paulo.

No concurso da última quinta-feira (10), nenhuma aposta acertou a faixa principal e o valor acumulou.

O g1 transmite todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube .

A aposta mínima para a Mega-Sena custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online .

Volante da Mega-Sena — Foto: Ana Marin/g1

As apostas podem ser realizadas até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

Ainda segundo a Caixa, para os sorteios realizados aos domingos as apostas simples podem ser efetuadas até as 22h de sábado por meio das unidades lotéricas, pelo Portal Loterias Caixa e do aplicativo Loterias Caixa.

A comercialização dos Bolões Caixa nos canais eletrônicos, nesse caso, acontece até às 10h45 do domingo, quinze minutos antes da realização dos sorteios.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: Son of notorious Somali dictator reportedly living in Ohio decades after brutal regime's collapse
articles.summary: Ayanle Siad Barre, son of Somalia's former dictator, has been living in Ohio's large Somali community, prompting calls for a U.S. investigation.
articles.body: The son of former Somali dictator Mohamed Siad Barre, whose brutal regime was accused of widespread atrocities during his more than two decades in power, has been living in Ohio for years, according to a new report. Ayanle Siad Barre, 61, lives in the Columbus area, home to a large Somali community, the New York Post reported. The outlet also identified his sister, Deka Mohamed Siad, as living in Ohio. Their father ruled Somalia from 1969, until his government was overthrown in 1991. His regime has been accused of mass killings that left as many as 200,000 people dead, torture and other human rights abuses, including atrocities against the Isaaq clan. Mohamed Siad Barre died in 1995. Historian and Oxford University doctoral researcher Mohamed Haji Ingiriis described Ayanle as his father's "right-hand man" and alleged that he wielded significant power within the government, according to the Post. Fox News Digital has not independently verified those allegations. TRUMP DOJ ESCALATES CITIZENSHIP CRACKDOWN ON GROUP ACCUSED OF HIDING TERROR TIES, VIOLENT CRIMES Fox News Digital previously reported that another figure from the Barre era, former Somali military commander Yusuf Abdi Ali, had lived in the U.S. before being deported. An immigration judge determined in 2024 that Ali personally engaged in torture while serving in the Somali National Army, and ordered soldiers under his command to detain and torture civilians and assist in extrajudicial killings, according to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Ali, who had been living as a permanent resident in Virginia, was deported to Somalia in December 2024. "The United States will not be a safe haven for those who commit human rights violations," ICE official Russell Hott said at the time. EX-PHILIPPINE PRESIDENT DUTERTE TO FACE TRIAL ON CRIMES AGAINST HUMANITY CHARGES The Post also reported that Ayanle established a translation-services company called Somal Global Services. His sister, Deka, and her late husband operated Vanguard Home Health Care, which received more than $1.8 million in Medicare funding, according to documents reviewed by the publication. The Post reported that the company appeared to have operated legitimately and filed the appropriate paperwork. Some survivors of the Barre regime are now calling for U.S. authorities to investigate members of the former dictator's family. Human rights activist Suleiman Bolaleh called for an investigation to determine what Barre family members knew or did during the dictatorship, according to the Post. DOJ CHARGES 19 DEFENDANTS IN ALLEGED $4M PHILADELPHIA MEDICARE AND MEDICAID FRAUD The calls for an investigation do not establish wrongdoing by Ayanle or other family members. Fox News Digital reached out to Ayanle Siad Barre for comment, but attempts to reach him through publicly listed contact information were unsuccessful. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP ICE, Department of Justice and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment. Fox News Digital's Peter Pinedo contributed to this reporting.

articles.title: Houthi projectile wounds two, damages mosque in Jazan region, Saudi says
articles.summary: The Houthis say they carried out a strike targeting a Saudi military base in Sharurah, Najran province.
articles.body:
Saudi Civil Defence has said that two people were wounded and a mosque and several buildings were damaged after a projectile fired by the Yemeni Houthi rebels struck Saudi Arabia’s southern Jazan region.

Several vehicles were also damaged by the projectile that landed in Jazan’s al-Tuwal governorate on Saturday, it added.

A civil defence spokesperson called the targeting of civilian objects a “flagrant violation of international humanitarian law”, adding that established emergency procedures had been implemented.

Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi rebels said they carried out a strike targeting a Saudi military base in Sharurah, in the southern Najran province, using ballistic missiles and drones. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said in a post on X that the attack hit “weapons depots and command and control centres” and that the targeted sites were “managing the aggression against our nation and people”.

Saree, who did not state when the attack took place, warned Saudi Arabia that further military actions against Yemen would prompt larger, more intense strikes deeper inside Saudi territory.

Saudi Civil Defence later said the danger had passed in the Khamis Mushait governorate after a warning was issued for residents there.

The Iran-backed Houthis have launched missile and drone strikes on southern Saudi Arabia in recent days.

On Tuesday, the group struck civilian and economic facilities in Saudi cities of Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran, wounding 73 people, including women and children.

The strikes on the kingdom are part of a rapid escalation in Yemen’s long-running conflict, which reignited in July after roughly four years of relative calm under a United Nations-brokered truce.

Houthi fighters have taken control of Yemen’s entire Red Sea coast, seizing the strategic port city of Mocha, while Yemeni government forces have opened new fronts in al-Jawf, Marib and al-Bayda.

More than 500 people have been killed and tens of thousands displaced in the fighting, according to the International Organization for Migration and local officials.

The UN Security Council held an emergency session on the crisis this month, as Special Envoy Hans Grundberg warned Yemen faces “a new and more dangerous phase of war”.

articles.title: D4vd case explained: The allegations, evidence and latest developments in Celeste Rivas case
articles.summary: US Streamers News: A year after Celeste Rivas Hernandez’s remains were discovered inside a Tesla linked to singer D4vd, the case has entered a critical new phase. David .
articles.body: A year after Celeste Rivas Hernandez’s remains were discovered inside a Tesla linked to singer D4vd, the case has entered a critical new phase. David Anthony Burke, who performs as D4vd, is facing murder and other charges and has pleaded not guilty. His prominent defense lawyers have since withdrawn, his family is pursuing a civil case, and prosecutors continue to present serious allegations that Burke disputes.What prosecutors allege in the D4vd and Celeste Rivas caseThe case began attracting national attention in September 2025, when Celeste’s remains were found in the front trunk of a Tesla registered to Burke’s address. Prosecutors later alleged that Celeste had gone to Burke’s Hollywood Hills home in April 2025 and that he killed her there.Those claims became central during a preliminary hearing in July. Prosecutors presented messages, photographs and other evidence as they argued that Burke had been involved with Celeste while she was underage. A judge subsequently ruled that there was enough evidence for the case to proceed to trial. Burke has maintained his not-guilty plea.Prosecutors have also alleged that Celeste threatened to expose her relationship with Burke shortly before her death. They have argued that this gave Burke a possible motive for the killing.The defense has challenged that narrative. Burke’s lawyers previously argued that prosecutors had no eyewitness or camera footage showing Celeste entering his home during the period in which they allege she was killed. Those arguments form part of the defense case as the proceedings move forward.D4vd’s lawyers withdraw as Celeste’s family seeks death penaltyOne of the biggest recent developments came at the end of August, when Burke’s high-profile legal team withdrew from the case. Blair Berk, Marilyn Bednarski and Regina Peter were replaced by attorneys from the Los Angeles County Public Defender’s Office after the court determined Burke qualified for appointed counsel. No specific reason for the withdrawal was publicly given.Burke entered another not-guilty plea and is now represented by a public defender. His next scheduled court proceeding is October 19, while the trial is expected to take place later.The case has also moved into civil court. Celeste’s parents, Mercedes Martinez and Jesus Rivas, have filed a wrongful-death lawsuit against Burke and several people connected to him. The lawsuit alleges that others enabled or facilitated the relationship between Burke and Celeste. Those claims are separate from the criminal case and remain allegations.As the anniversary of Celeste’s death approached, her parents publicly called for the death penalty if Burke is convicted. They said:“If the death penalty were activated, it would be perfect for this kind of human being, devoid of feelings and emptiness inside, and without conscience, who only caused pain to our daughter, our family, and the world that supports our precious daughter,”The decision on whether prosecutors will seek capital punishment rests with Los Angeles County authorities, not the family.For now, Burke remains in custody while the criminal case moves toward trial. The allegations against him have not been proven in court, and the proceedings will determine how prosecutors’ evidence and the defense’s challenges are ultimately weighed.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
